title: Flow review duplicates: complete same-run evidence per pair and scoped consumer rewiring (review v2 slices 3-4 subset)
description: Owner ask 2026-09-17: the evidence-based review (including evidence from earlier versions, eneo-ve7i) must also find duplicated work and prepare the improvement. Astra design (session eneo-review-cross-version-design iteration 2, max, green 8). Verified in source on tidy 50849fe8e: ai_builder_flow_review_suggestions.py ~:566 admits duplicated_work with one cited source from any named step and no common run (test_ai_builder_flow_review_suggestions.py ~:185 accepts step 1 output plus step 2 instruction); ReviewEditScope (ai_builder_flow_review.py ~:737, effect guard ~:874) lets only named steps change, so a fold cannot rewire consumers; investigation excerpts are filtered to named steps (~:646). Design: (1) evidence contracts per kind: duplicated_work = both steps' instructions, actual inputs and complete outputs from the same completed run (quotes stay highlights, re-validated at investigation); repeated_prompt_pattern = shared wording alone, never upgraded to duplicated work, and the same prompt on different inputs is not foldable; redundant_context = recorded inputs show repeated material, and a proposal must name the exact material and how every affected consumer keeps its obligations (covers eneo-b7j part c). (2) Separate read scope from edit scope: producers may change; affected consumers get only the server-derived reference/binding substitutions the fold needs, enforced before compilation and on the resulting diff; validate the whole compiled definition (dangling references, changed implicit-source selection, contracts, output obligations). (3) Observation vs actionable decided on the server: mismatched or added consumers make the finding observation-only with the reason shown; the model never grants itself edit authority. (4) Pack complete groups under review_request_budget through eneo-8hn's fitting owner; insufficient budget withholds the actionable claim; caps and one review call unchanged. (5) Historical groups are enabled in eneo-ve7i's activation slice; 'verified improvement' only after eneo-4x2 immutable candidate execution plus eneo-d99 verdicts. Allowed backend files: ai_builder_flow_review.py, ai_builder_flow_review_sample.py, ai_builder_flow_review_suggestions.py, ai_builder_service.py, ai_builder_edit_proposal.py; step_lineage.py and existing compiler/validation helpers only where required. Tests: genuine duplicate folded with consumer rewired and required output preserved; same prompt on different inputs gives no fold; changed or added consumer refuses the actionable suggestion but keeps a justified observation; incomplete, mixed-run, failed-only or lineage-less groups cannot authorize a fold; unrelated consumer prompt/configuration edits refused; implicit, prompt and template references correct after removal and renumbering; one provider-backed discovery check (validator acceptance is not discovery evidence). Do not build: a generic optimizer, similarity index, automatic removal from matching prompts, another graph/rewriter or replay engine, per-model heuristics, larger budgets to force evidence through, token-saving claims for zero-token renderers or reorganized per-item calls.

title: Stream flow-step completions so proxy idle timeouts cannot cut long generations
description: Run 23307d61 (2026-09-15 13:43 CEST, flow f96e8648) step 2 failed flow_provider_unavailable after 125.7 s: HAProxy in front of https://gpu.sundsvall.se returned its 504 page (timeout server ~2 min) while vLLM completed at 13:45:31 with 200 OK. Non-streaming completion sends nothing for the whole generation, so every inactivity timeout on the path (HAProxy client/server, any NAT) is a hard ceiling on answer length. Infra mitigation: timeout server/client 900s on that HAProxy. Durable fix: flow-step completions stream through the same provider-call owner the Builder already uses (silence-bounded deadline, see ai-builder-streaming-silence-deadline-20260911), so a token flows every few hundred ms; keep the step deadline as the only Eneo-side ceiling. Also confirm litellm.Timeout from a proxy 504 maps to provider_unavailable retryable=True (it did here). Evidence: worker log 11:45:30Z error_type=Timeout, exception body '504 Gateway Time-out The server didn't respond in time.'

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
2026-09-16 21:15 Astra orchestration review 3 (score 7) ranks this FIRST by ROI (strongest documented failure evidence), then capacity, then immutable draft execution (eneo-9os), hygiene, test cases (eneo-427). Design constraints, verified in source by Claude:
- Flow steps call the provider with an observer and stream=False; completion_service.py:730 raises when stream and an observer are combined; provider_call_observer.py:177 hardcodes "stream": False in request evidence; the adapter's _observed_provider_call (tenant_model_adapter.py:1564) owns started/completed/unknown receipts.
- Do NOT bypass the observer or add a second provider path. Stream internally beneath the existing complete-response contract and reconstruct one terminal response. Preserve provider-reported usage, outcome-unknown on interruption, cancellation, the shared step deadline, and reject truncated streams. Never expose partial streamed text as a completed step. Update the request evidence stream flag.
- Streaming reduces silence during generation only; it cannot help if the proxy times out during queueing, prefill or buffering before the first token.
- Before ranking it above capacity, check whether the HAProxy 900 s mitigation recorded above was deployed and take one correlated long-call trace; if the mitigation is live, urgency drops.
ORDER on the step-execution path: streaming -> P1a snapshot reader -> runtime capacity packaging (1c), serialized, each rebased on the stable preceding interface. Streaming may run in parallel with Builder budgeting (1b) when write sets stay separate.

title: Step-focused edit must not scale its context with flow size (40+ steps)
description: Owner 2026-09-14 14:30: editing one step of a 40-step flow must not overwhelm the model. The eneo-z5u projection sends the target in full, its producer contracts, its consumer requirements, and ONE orientation list of every other step (number, name, mode). Producers and consumers are bounded by the graph, but the orientation list grows linearly with the flow, and consumer requirements can too on a fan-out step. Proposed shape to MEASURE before adopting (memory: deleting context has changed planner quality before, 52 vs 58 on the attachment cohort): keep producers and consumers in full; give names only for a bounded window around the target plus any step the target's own instructions reference; replace the rest with a count sentence ('Flödet har 40 steg, du ändrar steg 17'). Acceptance: input tokens flat as step count grows, no drop in successful target repairs or downstream validity on paired edit runs over a 10-step and a 40-step flow. Needs a large-flow fixture, which does not exist yet.
close_reason: LANDED on tidy ab2b6469f (commit 1be747b7d, owner ruling 08:10 'do the cost issue'): unrelated steps are listed as {step_number, name}; producers and consumers keep their contracts; flow.step_count added. Measured (round 2 receipt): prompt tokens per unrelated step 62/77 -> 20/25 (Luna/gemma), -9.2%/-13.9% at 30 steps, 36/36 first pass, reference-by-name edit resolves 6/6. DECISION recorded, not built: a flat projection (bounded window + count sentence) would also drop names outside the window and lose reference-based edits, the capability Astra reproduced on 5d427fb81; a message-based reference parser is the token-rule class the program deleted in 2.1-S. Residual cost is one short entry per step (about 20-25 tokens); revisit only if 100+ step flows appear. Gate step-context-index-gate green 8 after 5 passes (1: measurement, 2: instruction values, 3: ledger values, 4: lane collision + integration diagnosis, 5: green). ANSWER to the owner's hypothesis: previous + current + next is INSUFFICIENT. Use the target's DIRECT producers and consumers (one hop is the right default: for A->B->C, changing A leaves B's declared output and C's declared input unchanged, and full-flow validation checks every edge), plus complete server-side validation of the merged flow; do NOT send a transitive closure. Delete the positional window entirely: include names and numbers alongside actual dependencies plus a flow-count sentence. Per-mode context: renderer = actual body source, input/output types and delivery config (a renderer does NOT inherently consume the whole flow); template fill = exact bindings, template identity and control metadata, required scalar paths and types; review checkpoint = target policy, reviewed output contract, relevant producer policy; form/runtime input = referenced fields with types/requiredness/constraints, all applicable fields for whole-input reads. TWO DEFECTS Claude missed, both reproduced by local probe: (P1) an incompatible IMPLICIT JSON consumer passes both authoring checks (producer's required output changed summary -> different while its previous_step JSON consumer still requires summary; validate_spec and _validate_saved_step_consumers both pass, only runtime input validation fails; flow_validators.py:798 returns immediately for previous_step) so the downstream safety this slice claims is incomplete for implicit chaining; (P2 of the pair) the dependency projection misses runtime aliases and whole-input reads ('{{ föregående_steg }}' projects no producer, '{{ flow_input }}' with a declared form field projects no form fields; ai_builder_flow_context.py:105). (P2) Deleting the orientation list CANNOT deliver flat cost on its own: the scoped tool schema still requires the complete ordered list and enumerates every permitted keep reference, and repairs replay previous tool arguments, so untouched steps still cost input tokens, output tokens and repair context. ORDERED SLICES: (1) dependency and contract correctness (ai_builder_flow_context.py, shared reference analysis, flow_validators.py; adjacent template_reference_analyzer.py, ai_builder_validation_references.py, ai_builder_edit_proposal.py) - complete alias/whole-input projection, reject incompatible implicit JSON chains before a proposal is approvable; (2) remove the model's unchanged-step round trip (edit_tool_schema, plan_edit_context, edit_proposal, edit_compiler, request preparation) - admit ONE target modification, server-expand, compile and validate, identities/order/revision checks intact; (3) reduce orientation context WITH measurement, degree-aware not 'flat with flow size'; (4) user recovery and publication copy (typed-failure change SEPARATE from the UI copy/entry change). Next: slice 1 to an Astra worker.

title: Flow editor autosave drops edits made during an in-flight save and self-collides with stale_revision
description: Reported 2026-09-15 by a colleague: while selecting 5-6 items in the flow editor the toast 'Flödet ändrades av en annan användare. Dina ändringar beräknas mot den nya versionen.' fires repeatedly and only one of the six selections survives; the colleague asked for a classic Save button. Root cause (tidy 9340dc05f, same on dev image 88e3d1e): (1) FlowEditor.scheduleAutoSave fires editor.saveChanges() 500 ms after every change with no in-flight guard, so a second full PATCH /flows/{id} is sent while the first is still running; (2) PATCH /flows/{id} carries no expected_revision, FlowRepository.update fences on the draft_revision read at request start, so the second request of the same user hits the fence and gets 400 stale_revision with the 'another user' text; (3) ResourceEditor.saveChanges snapshots update at save start and, for a full save, replaces update with the server response on completion (applyUpdates field=undefined returns the server copy), so every edit made during the flight is discarded even when no conflict occurs. Fix at the owner (ResourceEditor, shared by Flow/Assistant/App/GroupChat/SpaceSettings editors): serialize saves (one in flight, coalesce later changes into one follow-up save), and merge the server response three-way so fields edited during the flight keep the local value and are saved next; FlowEditor re-points _temp_ step ids to the real ids by assistant_id after each save (it already does this for the active step only). Server: PATCH /flows/{id} should accept expected_revision from the editor so the fence reflects what the editor saw, and the stale_revision message must not claim 'another user' when the caller collided with itself. Keep autosave; a Save button would keep the same clobber on the explicit save path (FlowEditor.flushFlowSaves uses the same saveChanges). Tests: ResourceEditor concurrent-save ordering and three-way merge; FlowEditor.test.ts 'classifies each overlapping save' must be revisited since overlapping saves no longer happen.

title: Edit approval carries the pre-preparation diff, not the plan the user approves
description:
Found by the Codex commit gate (session review-suggestions-gate, iteration 21, 2026-09-06) while gating the review-edit scope. Pre-existing and NOT specific to review turns: it affects every AI Builder edit.

In ai_builder_edit_proposal.process_edit_arguments, compile_edit_proposal produces both the compiled spec and an approval whose FlowEditDiff describes that compiled spec. prepare_compiled_spec_for_session then runs (ai_builder_compiled_spec_preparation.py:49), which disambiguates duplicate step names and canonicalizes resources, and its output replaces the spec. The approval is then copied forward with the ORIGINAL diff and returned beside the final spec. So the diff the user is shown can describe a plan that is not the plan they are approving. test_ai_builder_compiled_spec_preparation.py:390 proves preparation renames the second of two duplicate-named steps.

Codex's smallest safe correction: derive the effective diff from the current flow and the final prepared spec, and place that same diff in the approval; keep the authored-proposal check for model feedback. current_flow_authoring_spec() builds the baseline and _build_step_changes() (ai_builder_edit_compiler.py:587) computes the changes, so the pieces exist; _build_step_changes would need to become public.

What is already closed on review turns (commit for slice 2b): validate_review_edit_effect holds the COMPILED diff to the review scope, and review_edit_renamed_outside_the_scope refuses a preparation-time rename of a step the findings do not name. Those bound the review path; they do not fix the disclosure defect for ordinary edits.

Acceptance: the FlowEditDiff in the approval describes the spec actually returned, with a test that makes preparation rename a step and asserts the approval reports it.

title: Content coverage: every deliverable the user enumerated reaches the plan's output contract
description: Evidence (172-case 3a leg, 84 missed expected field groups): 15 groups were cited by the classifier as named results but dropped by the planner; 25 were never cited (enumerations in prose the classifier did not read as the result's contents); 22 were cited as clauses (A0-Q2 fixes the naming). Design: (1) admission: a proposal whose steps carry no leaf for a cited named result is repaired or refused at the result contract (ai_builder_result_contract / proposal admission), so the planner cannot drop a cited deliverable; (2) reader recall: the classifier prompt's named_result rule reads 'flödet ska ta fram X, Y och Z' as the result's contents when the terminal output is structured or a report; (3) the 'no JSON step' cases (a text reply built without a structured analysis step) are architecture, measured separately. Measure on the leaf-fields cohort x3 + broad x1. Slice E (m55.24) is not needed: the citation mechanism exists.

comments.text: Root cause found 2026-09-04: named_result_projection (ai_builder_action_policy.py) returns None unless terminal_output is structured_json, so for report, text and DOCX/PDF flows the cited deliverables are only a prompt rule ('include every final-report fact in the source-reading JSON output_fields') with no admission check; the 'cited but plan missing' losses are almost all report flows. Design: extend the projection to every terminal whose plan has a structured step feeding the writer (the cited names must appear as leaves of that step), keep the JSON-terminal rule as is, and measure on the leaf-fields cohort.

comments.text: Design detail from source (2026-09-04): the one verification predicate exists (_verify_attested_result_contract in ai_builder_proposal_intent.py at admission, _spec_satisfying_attested_contract in ai_builder_create_compiler.py as the compiled postcondition, both over the TERMINAL step's output_fields via attested_result_contract_violations). For report/text/DOCX/PDF terminals the terminal step has no output_fields, which is why named_result_projection stands down. Extension: (1) named_result_projection also projects for report terminals; (2) the predicate verifies against the verification step = the terminal when it declares output_fields, else the last structured step before the terminal (the source-reading JSON step the writer consumes); (3) the prompt rule names that step instead of 'the FINAL step'; (4) the compiler postcondition uses the same step choice. One owner for 'which step carries the attested contract' shared by prompt, admission and postcondition. Measure on the leaf-fields cohort.

title: Cited nullability for user-named results: carry the fact through evidence, projection, admission and the postcondition
description:

Codex gate lane-smart-bwi-gate (passes 1 and 2) direction: nullability must be a cited tri-state (allowed | forbidden | unspecified) persisted on NamedResultEvidence, transported by ObligatedResultKey / ProposalObligationProjection, retained on AttestedResultField, and verified by BOTH admission and _spec_satisfying_attested_contract (which today strips "null" in _schema_field_type, so nullability drift is invisible).

The reader that would extract the fact is the slot classifier, so this carries a classifier-contract change, a persisted planning-state field with a schema-version and older-session degradation decision, and its own measurement.

Acceptance: user evidence lacks null permission and the proposal says nullable -> rejected, or compiled non-null; user evidence permits null and the proposal omits it -> rejected, or compiled nullable; tampering the compiled schema in either direction is detected by the postcondition.

title: Dictated JSON input: no input_contract is emitted when the user describes the payload without a schema
description:
Evidence (advanced_explicit legs, 2026-09-06): advanced_explicit_open_eplatform_mapping and advanced_explicit_integration_validation both dictate an incoming JSON contract ("Inkommande payload och utgående resultat ska ha separata kontrakt", "Flödet tar emot JSON från en kommunal integration"). The compiled plan has the right step (input_source flow_input, input_type json) but its input_contract is None in 3/3 observations on both the parent and the candidate arm, so the harness check expected_input_contract_schema fails and the runtime validates nothing.

Cause: _apply_flow_input_schema only fills input_contract from a resolved declared input schema (SchemaEvidence). When the user describes the payload without pasting a schema, nothing is emitted.

Decision needed before implementing: what a truthful contract is when the payload's fields are unknown. Options include a permissive object contract, a contract derived from the fields the user did name, or asking one discovery question. Inventing field names is not acceptable.

description: Owner ask 2026-09-15: Granska med AI-byggaren should make a working-but-badly-built flow (example: IBIC package, 14 steps) more token- and step-efficient, fold duplicated steps and split oversized ones, without losing detail or quality, verified on previous runs. title: Builder asks whether the transcript should label speakers (vemsa diarization)
description:
Owner request 2026-09-03 (after wiring vemsa to the :8144 lane): when a brief needs a transcription step and the tenant's transcription service is configured for diarization, the Builder should ask whether the transcript should mark who says what, and build the whole speaker experience when the answer is yes.

Design (fits commit 3a's interaction policy table):
- Slot 'speaker_identification' in ai_builder_slot_interaction_policy.py, values label_speakers | plain_transcript. Relevant only when primary_runtime_input is audio AND the transcription service is configured with mode diarize (settings flag flow_transcription_service_configured + mode passed into the discovery context; not relevant otherwise, so tenants without vemsa never see it). when_unknown = ask. has_explicit_text = wording about speakers/participants (vem som säger vad, talare, deltagare) makes it an ask, never a silent default. No preselection (owner UI decision).
- Question catalog entry (Swedish): 'Ska transkriptet märka upp vem som säger vad?' with options 'Ja, märk upp talarna' / 'Nej, löpande text'; one-line helper that names are mapped from a participants field.
- Materialization (flow_draft_materialization.py already writes wizard.transcription_enabled + transcription_model from default_transcription_model_id): also write wizard.transcription_diarization from the slot. When label_speakers: add a participants list form field ('Vilka deltog?') and a speaker_mapping step after the transcription step, mirroring the editor template in FlowEditor.ts (participantsField, buildSpeakerMappingOutputConfig, review_policy edit); later prompt steps reference the named speakers.
- Frontend: the Builder question card renders the two options with the existing shadcn option control; the created flow opens with Talaridentifiering on in stage 2.
- Tests: relevance off without the service; asked with audio + service; explicit speaker wording asks; every assume writes plain_transcript; materialization writes metadata + participants field + speaker_mapping step; runtime parity with the editor-built flow.

Lands after A0 commit 3a (Beads m55.21) because the policy table is the owner.

title: Honor explicit step inputs in frontend type-chain validation
description:
Problem: imported flows that explicitly project JSON from an earlier step are incorrectly rejected when the immediately preceding step outputs PDF. Backend has_explicit_underlag already gives bindings precedence; frontend getFlowStepValidationIssues does not. Owner: existing flowStepTypes validation and flowUnderlag binding inspection. Scope: align frontend chain checks with explicit question/source_refs semantics, regression tests for earlier JSON sources and absent/empty bindings, preserve actual implicit-chain errors and global rules. No backend/runtime, model prompts, schema, or data changes. Acceptance: exported IBIC package validates unchanged; explicit JSON source_refs work after PDF and with all_previous_steps; empty bindings keep implicit validation. Verify nearest flow validation tests, frontend typecheck/lint and repository hooks. Risk: over-skipping checks for invalid bindings; retain separate binding validation. Recovery: revert focused code commit. User authorizes commit and push to refactor/flows-tidy-ai-builder.

## Steps to Reproduce
Import a flow whose final text writer has JSON input and source_refs projecting fields from an earlier JSON step, while the immediately preceding step renders PDF. The editor reports typed_io_incompatible_type_chain and marks JSON as legacy-invalid although the selected underlag supplies JSON.

## Acceptance Criteria
Use existing getFlowStepUnderlag to align implicit-chain checks and input-type options with explicit bindings. Keep first-step/global constraints and implicit PDF-to-JSON rejection. Prove the old failure then pass nearest binding, type, config, template and transition tests; pass frontend typecheck/lint and commit hooks. Push the focused fix to refactor/flows-tidy-ai-builder without modifying unrelated work.

RED reproduced five failures; GREEN 136 affected tests, eslint, svelte-check 0 errors/0 warnings, original 16-step package validates unchanged with a valid JSON option. No provider or backend changes.

title: Direct-compose reports render 'Extraktionsvarningar: []' on every clean source section
description: Found in the owner-ordered line-by-line re-judgement of the landed D worker output (05c5d9781). The direct-composition item template written by document_report/topology._compose_source_record_item_template always contains the line 'Extraktionsvarningar: {extraction_warnings}' (or 'Extraction warnings: ...'), and the runtime renderer _render_source_ref_value / _source_ref_value_to_text (runtime/step_input_resolution.py) renders list values via json.dumps, so a clean source (empty warnings list) renders 'Extraktionsvarningar: []' in the final report and a degraded one renders the raw JSON list of codes. The compiler test asserts the template string, not a rendered section. Fix (Claude): the item renderer drops a template line whose placeholders all rendered empty, an empty list renders as nothing, and a list of strings renders as a comma-separated list; tests for the renderer and one rendered per-source section with and without a warning. Ownership: runtime/step_input_resolution.py (renderer) + tests; the topology template stays.

title: Evidence-driven flow review: analyze a flow's runs in the Builder edit session and propose verified improvements
description: Owner decision 2026-09-04: keep it small. One review task, one model call, typed ranked findings each quoting evidence and proposing an edit (unused step output, duplicated steps, instruction versus outcome drift, cost concentration). title: Upstream LiteLLM: reasoning_effort mapping must keep the thinking budget below max_tokens or reject explicitly
description: Found 2026-09-17 in slice B of eneo-nb0 (LiteLLM 1.101.0). AnthropicConfig maps reasoning_effort for non-adaptive models to thinking.budget_tokens (litellm/llms/anthropic/chat/transformation.py ~:1594) without clamping to max_tokens, so requests with a cap at or below the mapped budget (captured: cap 512 or 4096 -> budget 4096) are rejected by Anthropic. The SDK's cap_thinking_budget_to_max_tokens (~:1290) is not called on that path, and calling it alone is not enough because it drops thinking when the cap is below the minimum budget. Eneo's decided behaviour (Astra ruling) is to send the bounded cap and the selected effort unchanged and surface the provider rejection. Upstream fix should keep both controls valid when possible or raise an explicit error; after it ships, bump the pinned LiteLLM version and re-run the reasoning tests. No local SDK patch.

title: AI Builder: bound attachment reading by observed provider throughput or remember classifier failures per session
description: After a classification provider failure the next turn packs the same attachments and waits out the same timeout before asking. comments.text: Fine-details (Astra 2026-09-13): a failed request does not prove the attachments caused it (rate limit, unsupported parameter, unknown outcome are distinguished by the failure contract ~310; send admission ~89 protects unknown outcomes): never cache a 'bad file' fingerprint after an arbitrary provider failure; ordinary retry keeps the same evidence. Continuing without a document is an EXPLICIT changed request that records the omitted evidence and rebuilds confirmation, named in the UI (which file could not be assessed, what remains unresolved). Relevance: bounded deterministic excerpts around explicit matches in the attachment-context owner, keep inventory and coverage, preserve source boundaries, remeasure tokens (equal chars != equal tokens). title: AI Builder request budget: proportional answer allocation replaces full-ceiling reservation
description: d952366ce reserved the model's full declared output ceiling before fitting input, which refuses every model whose catalogue output limit equals its window (974/2723 LiteLLM chat entries incl. Mistral, Grok, Azure GPT-5.1 chat, Ollama) and breaks two flows integration tests on the 8000/4096 fixture. Replace with one allocation owner: required input measured with the conservative counter, answer reserve = min(ceiling, ceil(share * room after required input)) with share a dimensionless deployment policy (default 1/2), optional input packed into the rest, provider max_tokens = min(ceiling, room after the packed input). Refuse only when required input leaves no room or exceeds the tenant input cap. Review gains the length guard. Codex session ai-builder-budget-rule-validation passes 1-2 (scores 5, 6) agree with the direction; next review is the implementation gate.

title: Flow drift check misses a changed model route: execution snapshot ignores the model name that tenant routes are built from
description: Found by the Astra failed-run recovery design (2026-09-17) and verified in source on tidy 50849fe8e: flows/assistant_execution_snapshot._completion_model_execution_surface hashes only the model id and litellm_model_name, but tenant models store litellm_model_name = None (tenant_model_service ~:269, route built at runtime from provider_type + name) and allow renaming name (~:342, moves the route). So an admin who changes a tenant model's name to another provider model keeps the same execution surface hash, the executor's drift check passes, and published flows silently run a different model, against the owner's no-silent-model-switch rule. Fix at the canonical snapshot owner: include the actual resolved route and execution-affecting settings in the execution identity (display names excluded); old evidence that cannot establish identity is classified honestly (for recovery: ineligible). title: Capability snapshot: narrow a persisted control on provider refusal evidence
description: Follow-up to the sampling-control retry. The persisted SupportedModelKwargs snapshot is the request-shape authority, but discovery (LiteLLM get_supported_openai_params) marks temperature tunable for GPT-5-class and o-series models that accept only the default, so every Builder call on such a model pays one refused round trip (~2 s) until an admin turns the control off. Design: when a provider refuses a control by name (unsupported_parameter/unsupported_value), persist a narrowed snapshot on the tenant model row with evidence provider_discovered (never widened again), through the tenant model service; the chat adapter and the flow runtime send the same controls and would benefit. Operator workaround today: disable temperature on the model in the tenant model admin (admin_explicit evidence).

comments.text: Codex design pass 2026-09-11 (gpt-6-astra xhigh, session ai-builder-budget-rule-validation, iteration 13): changes_required, score 6. Blockers before any implementation: (1) POLICY: an unsupported_value refusal of one value (e.g. temperature=0.0) does not establish the control is unsupported; either retain typed observations (parameter, value, code, phase) and only learn from parameter-level evidence, or name conservative suppression as an explicit operational policy (owner decision). (2) Narrowing must target the exact tenant-owned, non-deleted row with a conditional atomic update keyed on the observed model/provider revision (CompletionModelRepository reads include global rows; admin edits can race). (3) tenant_model_service.update refreshes capabilities whenever 'reasoning' is present in the payload, which the admin UI always sends (draft.ts:242): an unrelated admin save would rediscover and restore the refused control; refresh only on a real route/reasoning change. (4) Observation collection must be independent of retry admission and proposal telemetry (review path and budget-denied refusals would be missed); pass one bounded observation collection through Builder calls, persist best-effort once per model after execution. (5) A fourth evidence tag is rejected by current readers, which then resolve ALL optional controls as unsupported: readers must ship before writers (deployment order) or the tag must be avoided. (6) Widening ProviderCapabilityRejectedException.capability requires updating tenant_model_adapter.py:1597 (records every capability rejection as response_format_rejected) and must not activate the runtime's response_format fallback. Design brief: scratchpad design-capability-narrowing.md. Decision needed from the owner on (1) before implementing.

title: Make semantic proposal repair converge without terminal errors
description:
TL;DR: A valid Flow architecture can still terminate during proposal self-correction when a compositional text step fails to consume all relevant structured predecessors. Preserve the critic and make the canonical typed repair path converge generally, without case-, prompt-, filename-, or corpus-keyed behavior.

Problem and evidence

Report-layout R4 candidate C1 produced `self_correction_quality_failure` with typed code `final_text_step_must_reference_relevant_structured_outputs` on an otherwise valid document-to-DOCX-template architecture. Exact parent completed the same control first pass. The same exact candidate completed it first pass in R3, so the failure is provider-plan variance reaching a real fail-closed repair seam, not evidence of a deterministic report-layout transformation defect. R4 stopped before repeats and all 172-case legs. Immutable receipt and verdict identities are recorded on measurement task `eneo-flow-ai-builder-production-readiness-m55.5`.

Why it matters

The user sees a terminal Builder error after answering a valid canonical question. A retry may succeed, but relying on provider luck violates the production no-hard-failure gate. Weakening the critic would allow under-bound plans and is not acceptable.

Current and proposed canonical ownership

The typed invariant remains owned by `ai_builder_critic_invariants.py`. Failure classification remains owned by proposal finalization. Repair convergence should remain in the existing proposal self-correction/retry owner; do not add a second repair service, a case-specific compiler branch, or another prompt-only fallback. First determine whether the correct smallest complete solution is better typed repair feedback, a deterministic owner-level normalization already supported by the plan contract, or deletion/consolidation of a duplicate repair path.

Scope and non-goals

- Reproduce the generic topology class from typed plan contracts, not from the benchmark wording or fixture.
- Inventory preserved receipt incidence for this exact failure code across parent/candidate history and distinguish deterministic source behavior from provider variance.
- Add behavior-first RED proof at the stable proposal finalization/retry boundary.
- Implement only a general canonical-owner correction that preserves compiler, critic, source-evidence, architecture, and no-retry contracts.
- Do not change report-layout questions, corpus, fixtures, expectations, benchmark adjudication, provider model, broad classifier authority, or failure floors.

title: Expose source-local extraction warnings to document readers

including `pdf_text_likely_reversed`, but provider-visible source text contains
only the source marker, filename, and extracted body. The warning survives in
diagnostics and runtime metadata but is absent from the model input.

describe the degradation without preserving the canonical warning. R13 direct
C1 produced a complete six-source report but breached visible-degradation and
source-association floors for exactly this causal reason.

Canonical owner: `step_input_resolution.py`, which already detects the warning,
builds source-local diagnostics/metadata, and formats provider-visible source
headers.

`babb85366cf33d3ca2588124f81b223206a41313` slice onto the exact current product
candidate. Add the bounded warning list to only the affected provider-visible
source header. Reuse the existing warning detection result, preserve the
diagnostic and metadata, and keep clean source prompts byte-stable where
practical.

Reuse/delete: reuse `_runtime_source_extraction_warnings` and
`_format_runtime_source_text`; calculate warnings once rather than detecting
them separately for prompt and diagnostics. Add no service, schema, setting,
provider heuristic, or compatibility path.

Non-goals: no OCR or extraction repair; no warning invention; no aggregate
warning repeated across sources; no Builder/classifier/topology change; no
case-, corpus-, filename-, source-count-, or language-keyed logic; no BANKED
corpus/harness edit; no push.

the affected source; empty-source behavior remains explicit; diagnostics and
runtime metadata remain unchanged; focused runtime tests, full Flow/AI Builder
suites, canonical Pyright, Ruff/format, exact-diff peer gate score >=8, and a
new frozen direct/O9/broad measurement protocol pass before landing.

degraded sources. Revert the independent commit if clean-source bytes,
source-local association, token bounds, or measured quality regress.

title: Require report layout before committing multi-source report architecture
description:
TL;DR: Prevent a new multi-source generated-report architecture from being committed before the user-owned report layout is resolved. Reuse the existing aggregation relevance predicate and canonical question catalog, deepen the architecture gate, and delete the duplicate relevance projection. Preserve irrelevant shapes and old prerelease commits.

## Problem and value

Per-source sections, synthesized overview, and both create different deterministic flow topologies. Current code can commit a relevant new architecture with report_disposition absent. Close that gap without broad smartness, phrase matching, defaults, or case-specific behavior.

## Canonical owners and allowed paths

Reuse report_disposition_is_relevant in ai_builder_aggregation_intent.py. Extend ai_builder_architecture_derivation.py for the new create-mode commit gate. Delete the duplicate helper in planning_state_builder.py. Limit behavior tests to existing action-policy, architecture-derivation, degraded-classifier, server-decision-dispatch, service, replay, and integration-session owners. be39ddbd65283e4c8abbf79cabe010a51a778e03 is evidence only; rebuild it on the synchronized baseline.

## Product contract

Require the field only for document input plus generated PDF or DOCX report output plus multiple or flexible document scope. Ask the existing canonical bilingual closed question when unresolved. Do not ask for single-source, non-document, non-report, DOCX template-fill, edit-mode, unknown-prerequisite, already-pending, or applied-plan shapes. Existing pinned commits with a missing value stay pinned; later commit-grade evidence may trigger existing revise_architecture behavior.

## Non-goals

No migration, compatibility reader, reopen or invalidation path, policy default, new service, retry, fallback, classifier compaction, phrase table, prompt-keyed rule, case ID, corpus key, source-count threshold, benchmark edit, or release change.

## Baseline and stopping rule

First merge origin/develop a243cbbe7e onto origin/refactor/flows-tidy-ai-builder a65083bac773 in an isolated worktree with a650 as first parent and record the exact baseline SHA. Build the candidate separately and record its SHA. Never touch BANKED 0.4 paths. No push is authorized. Any deterministic failure, peer score below 8, or frozen measurement-floor breach stops the slice.

## Acceptance Criteria

Exact baseline and candidate SHAs are recorded. New relevant create-mode architectures cannot commit without commit-grade report_disposition. Irrelevant and prerequisite cases remain unchanged. Existing commits with a missing value remain stable; later strong evidence revises through the existing drift owner. The duplicate relevance helper is deleted. title: Keep report topology channels aligned after lowering
description:
TL;DR: A valid multi-source report can terminate before proposal creation when document-report lowering changes a step's predecessor from TEXT to JSON but retains the previously derived input channel. Recompute the server-owned derived channel from final lowered adjacency so all supported report layouts compile without weakening typed validation.

## Problem and impact

R2 produced a hard `architecture_materialization_failed` for an explicit report whose classifier evidence and architecture commit were correct. The report lowerer replaced a weak TEXT section writer with a structured JSON section writer. A following retained JSON overview step still carried `underlag_channel=implicit_previous`, derived against the removed TEXT predecessor; the final JSON-to-TEXT boundary requires `whole_object`. This is a latent general compiler bug exposed by the new architecture gate, not a benchmark-specific miss.

## Ownership

- Current and proposed canonical owner: `ai_builder_assembly/document_report/lowering.py`, which owns the structural rewrite.
- Invariant owner to preserve: `ai_builder_assembly/plan.py::derive_underlag_channel` plus `FlowAssemblyPlan` validation.
- Reuse the existing derivation function after final report adjacency is known. Do not duplicate its rules, weaken validation, or create a generic repair service.

## Smallest complete slice

- Add a provider-neutral compiler behavior test for a reader JSON → weak section TEXT → retained overview JSON → terminal TEXT outline.
- Prove all non-null report dispositions remain valid after lowering, while the exact `both` shape produces the deterministic compose topology.
- Re-derive the server-owned underlag channel for lowered previous-step adjacency at the report-lowering boundary.

## Deliberate non-goals

- No classifier, prompt, question, architecture-gate, provider adapter, harness, corpus, fixture, expectation, runtime execution, UI, migration, or public API change.
- No case ID, phrase, filename, language token, model-output name, or report-specific exception in the typed validator.
- Do not cherry-pick unrelated historical aggregate-contract or extraction-warning candidates.

## Validation

- RED/GREEN focused compiler regression.
- Existing report-disposition compiler matrix and assembly-plan invariants.
- Full Flow AI Builder unit suite, full Flow unit suite, relevant integration tests, canonical Pyright, Ruff, format, diff check, and repository hooks.
- One exact-staged Codex xhigh peer gate before local commit. No push.

## Risk and rollback

Risk is bounded to server-owned report topology projection. Incorrect broad normalization could mask provider defects, so only the derived channel may change and the typed plan validator remains authoritative. Rollback is the single local commit; R2 receipts remain immutable and cannot be rerun under the same addendum.

title: Builder provider rejection leaves no identifying trace: unknown code and param are dropped, provider_expectation is a hardcoded placeholder
description: 2026-09-14 16:15 on the test server (build refactor-flows-tidy-ai-builder-2baa78c): editing an existing flow failed twice with planner_upstream_error / eneo_error_code 9024, azure/gpt-5.6-luna, provider 400 after ~1s on a 4962-token request in a 1050000-token window. Neither occurrence could be identified, because: (1) AIBuilderProviderRequestEvidence.to_log_value hardcodes provider_expectation={'source':'unavailable'} (ai_builder_error_contract.py:377) so that field never carries anything; (2) _PROVIDER_ERROR_CODES and _PROVIDER_ERROR_PARAMETERS are closed allowlists, so a code or param outside them is dropped silently and safe_detail carried neither; (3) provider_error_fields (ai_builder_provider_call.py:220) returns {} when the adapter kept no body and no consumed response. Ruled out by the numbers: context length, our deadline (deadline_reached false), and the native-strict subset (route supports_strict_tool_schema=false). Live candidates: the 2026-09-11 temperature refusal on this same model recurring in a shape the extractor cannot read (the 600fb10b1 retry only fires when the error names a SupportedModelKwargs control, and another_call_permitted was false); max_tokens=128000 refused by the deployment; parallel_tool_calls refused. Astra session provider-400-diagnosis-20260914 at xhigh is adjudicating and designing the durable fix. Acceptance: a provider rejection we do not recognise still names itself in the incident event, with no prompt, schema or credential text in logs.

comments.author: ccimen
comments.text: DESIGN 2026-09-14 16:27 (Astra xhigh, session provider-400-diagnosis-20260914, changes_required 7, artifact .codex/artifacts/codex-peer-loop-builder-edit-turn-provider-400-diagnosis-*.md). ROOT CAUSE OF THE INCIDENT: NOT identified, and Astra refused a causal green light without correlated provider evidence. It weakened two of my candidates by synthetic check against the INSTALLED SDK: LiteLLM 1.98.0 converts max_tokens 128000 into max_completion_tokens for Azure GPT-5 (gpt_5_transformation.py:255), so the wrong-parameter-name theory is out; and an ordinary unsupported_value/temperature response DOES survive the installed adapter and our extractor, so the incident carried a different envelope. Still live: the deployment's accepted token-limit VALUE, parallel_tool_calls, the edit schema. ROOT CAUSE OF THE EVIDENCE LOSS: REPRODUCED. provider_error_fields (ai_builder_provider_call.py:227) consults the buffered response only when error.body is not a Mapping; an EMPTY mapping is still a Mapping, so the fallback is skipped and code+param come back null even when the buffered response carries unsupported_value and temperature. MY CLAIMS CORRECTED: another_call_permitted is always false in the final classification (so it does not prove no retry ran); the fingerprint covers only stage/kind/status (so identical fingerprints do not mean identical causes); outcome_kind server_confirm_requirements does not identify the failing turn because the confirmation dispatcher makes no proposal call; unclassified_outgoing_field_count describes SDK input, not wire JSON; the packed figure is fixed_input_tokens 5669. REJECTED from my proposal: bounded provider MESSAGE excerpts, even behind an operator setting (a length limit does not stop prompts or credentials); and giving param the same freedom as code (paths carry user schema names). DECIDED: deepen ONE owner (provider_error_fields) into a typed rejection record with safe code, normalized param, extraction source/status, provider correlation id; delete provider_expectation rather than populate it. Lane fix/ai-builder-provider-rejection-evidence in worktree eneo-ai-builder-provider-evidence, worker impl-eneo-gs0 (astra high), spec at scratchpad/spec-eneo-gs0.md. Regression check: the range changes no provider envelope or dependency pin, but the failing turn was never correlated, so the range is neither blamed nor exonerated.

comments.author: ccimen
comments.text: LOCAL REPRODUCTION 2026-09-14 16:34 (Claude, real openai SDK + httpx.MockTransport against the installed backend venv, scratchpad/probe2.py). Results change the leading hypothesis. (1) An ordinary Azure temperature refusal (error.code=unsupported_value, error.param=temperature) is extracted CLEANLY by provider_error_fields, and identically whether stream=True or stream=False. So streaming is not the differentiator, and the production incident was NOT an ordinary temperature refusal: had it been, safe_detail would have carried provider_parameter=temperature and the 600fb10b1 retry hook would have had its named control. (2) Exactly two envelope shapes lose both facts: an APIM/gateway envelope {statusCode, message} with no error object, and an Azure error object carrying a message but no code and no param. Both produce code=None param=None, which is precisely what the incident logged. (3) Control shapes confirm the parser is otherwise fine: content_filter extracts its code, and an invalid_value/max_completion_tokens rejection extracts both. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX: the mapping-guard defect Astra reproduced is real but is NOT what happened here, because the SDK populates error.body from the same response it buffers, so the two agree. For this incident class the provider sent no machine-readable code at all, so no allowlist or envelope-fallback change can recover it. The ONLY thing that would have identified it is the provider correlation id from the response headers (apim-request-id / x-ms-request-id), which an Azure admin can look up server-side, plus an extraction status saying the provider sent no machine-readable code. That must become the primary requirement of this slice; the envelope fallback stays as secondary hardening. Astra's refusal to log message prose stands and is unaffected.

The production failure did NOT reproduce. Create: a Swedish markupplatelse description produced a 4-step DOCX template-fill plan with no questions, and created the flow. Edit: asking for a PDF instead of the Word template was understood at the confirm-requirements stage (the same stage and target_kind the production diagnostic named), the proposal came back with step 4 as Rendera PDF and the other three marked Oforandrat, and the turn completed. So the edit path on this commit is healthy against an OpenAI route; the production 400 remains specific to that Azure deployment, still unidentified, and still the reason this bead exists. comments.author: ccimen
comments.text: LANDED 2026-09-14 18:12 as d1400f2a2 on refactor/flows-tidy-ai-builder (pushed). Astra gate session provider-400-diagnosis-20260914 iterations 2-3 at xhigh, final green / MIN_SCORE 8; Astra independently ran all 11 new adapter/header cases. WHAT SHIPPED: provider_error_fields returns a ProviderRejection record (safe code, normalized parameter, extraction source and status, provider correlation id); the envelope guard now asks whether an envelope supplies a usable fact instead of whether it is a Mapping, so an empty body no longer hides a useful buffered response; the outgoing field inventory derives from the real request; provider_expectation is deleted rather than populated. GATE FINDING ACCEPTED (iteration 2, P1) and it was the case that mattered: the Builder forces streaming on every call, and LiteLLM's error conversion drops the original response while keeping the provider headers in error.litellm_response_headers, which the extractor did not read, so the correlation id would still have been lost in production while the test passed (the old test attached the response to a hand-built BadRequestError and bypassed the conversion). Confirmed independently in the installed LiteLLM: exception_mapping_utils.py computes litellm_response_headers via _get_response_headers at 2187 and sets it at 2504/2509. Fixed by adding that mapping as the final correlation source with the same 3-header allowlist and validator, contributing only the id; new azure_adapter_rejection_retains_correlation_id drives a real streamed 400 through the installed adapter and went 3 failed/3 passed -> 6 passed. NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY: no provider message prose recorded anywhere, not even bounded behind a setting; param does not get code's freedom; no change to temperature, token limits, parallel_tool_calls or any tool schema. The original production 400 REMAINS UNIDENTIFIED and status=absent means no machine-readable fact was recovered, not proof none was sent. Next occurrence should carry a correlation id an Azure admin can trace.

title: Flow steps accept a length-truncated model answer as a completed result
description: Found by the Astra streaming design pass (2026-09-17, finding 3) and verified in source on tidy 50849fe8e: TenantModelAdapter reduces the provider finish reason to Completion.stop = (finish_reason == 'stop') (~:1524), flows/runtime/step_execution_runtime.infer_finish_reason (~:1004) returns only stop or tool_calls, and output processing consumes the text, so an answer cut off by the output cap (finish_reason length) that is still valid text or JSON passes as a completed step. Slice B of eneo-nb0 lowers the cap to min(O, I - input) for large inputs, which makes this more likely. Fix per Astra: reject known incomplete output before tool execution or result consumption with a typed failure that keeps the reason, while the provider receipt stays completed when its terminal outcome is known. Model agnostic. Ask the slice B gate whether this must land with slice B.

comments.text: 2026-09-17 08:25 Astra window value review iter 1 (session eneo-nb0-window-value-review, high, score 6 on the current plan): RECOMMENDS B, two fields and one conservative rule. Admin enters the route's max input I and max output O; when a provider publishes only a shared window, use it as I; drop 'input = context window' from the help text. Budget: W = I is the combined request budget; reserve r = min(O, ceil(share * (W - s - q))), pack optional input within W - s - r, send output cap min(O, W - s - t); tenant input caps still apply; missing I or O stays an explicit failure. Never infer C = I + O universally. The third field only buys fuller use of separate-budget models (option C: W = C when supplied else I, never refuse on missing C). Findings: P1 missing-C refusal is an availability regression; P1 the original runtime mismatch remains (adapter gives all of I to input and can request all of O, so I = O = 128k overflows a shared window) -> runtime packaging must enforce input + output cap <= W at the completion boundary incl. repair calls; P2 'ready' must also exclude limits below the safety buffer, shared by list/default/send; P2 58a9635c6 stops substitutes but does not repair historically invented output limits. Dispositions: af188110b remove C from storage/API/form, keep the capacity owner and typed missing-limit errors; 58a9635c6 and 44ae713f8 keep; readiness keep but require I/O only and simplify; 72a4911f9 keep the capacity object and one availability rule minus the C requirement; frontend 12e29ddd8, 7ff803416, 476ca56f4, 08a09997b keep (independent user-control fixes). comments.text: 2026-09-17 08:30 Astra window value review iter 2 (owner question: window = input + output?): NO. Correct numbers can give a wrong sum: valid for documented separate budgets (GPT-5: 272k + 128k = 400k), invalid for a vLLM shared window (max_model_len 128k entered as 128k/128k would invent 256k), unknown for luna 922k/128k and gemma 128k/128k until their actual route or server config is checked, and double counting for admins following today's help text. The sum also loses the independent input bound (400k window could admit 300k input against I = 272k). Recommendation unchanged: two fields, conservative combined budget W = I, no third field required; cost is unused capacity on separate-budget models (GPT-5: 128k of 400k, 32%; luna about 12% if its real window is 1,050k). Optional declared window only if recovering that capacity matters, never blocking. Proposed form wording: Max input = 'Maximum input tokens accepted by this deployment. If the provider specifies only a shared context window, enter that value. Eneo reserves room for the response within this limit.' Max output = 'Maximum tokens this deployment allows for one generated response, including reasoning tokens where the provider counts them toward this limit. Eneo may request fewer tokens to fit the request.' Budget: refuse if W - s - q < 1; r = min(O, ceil(share * (W - s - q))); pack within W - s - r and tenant cap; send output cap min(O, W - s - t); same invariant in runtime packaging incl. repair calls. Awaiting owner decision: B (no window field) or C (optional, never-blocking window).

title: Builder: a failed force-new session leaves no session and no retry
description: Raised by gate pass 5 on the handoff UI (2026-09-06). FlowAIBuilderDriver.createSession resets the whole driver state (abort, #resetFlowState) before the POST; when the POST rejects it surfaces the error and rethrows with hasSession=false. Every force-new path shares this: the header 'Börja om' (FlowAIBuilder.svelte handleStartOver), BuilderTurnAlert's start-over, and the replace-edit confirmation (which since 1d8a4429b correctly refuses to open the step/review on rejection). The generic error surface (BuilderTurnAlert) offers only dismissal; after dismissal the host shows the no-session skeleton and only a page reload recovers. Owner: the driver's createSession + the host's no-session branch. Fix shape to weigh: keep the current session until the new one arrives (reset after the POST resolves), or on rejection re-run initialize(targetKind)/resume the previous session id, and give the error surface a retry that re-runs the captured launch (review or saved step). Add the test 'force-new fails once, succeeds on retry, reaches the requested destination without remounting'.
close_reason: Landed on refactor/flows-tidy-ai-builder as a8be2d517. createSession keeps what its reset replaced - the state plus the uncertain-turn fence - and puts it back when the create is refused, so every force-new path leaves the user on the session they had instead of the no-session skeleton; the session is published before the draft GET; the refused forced create is recorded against the exact error it installed so the create-mode alert keeps offering the retry while that error stands; the saved-step scope is owned by the session it was opened from; and both surfaces clear their composer context only once the replacement is real, with the header consuming the rejection. Tests (all RED-verified on 50a86976b): FlowAIBuilderDriver.test.ts 'keeps the session it has when a forced new one is refused, and retries onto it', 'keeps the uncertain turn fence when the fresh session is refused', 'keeps the refused start-over offer only while its own error stands'; FlowAIBuilder.dom.test.ts 'keeps offering the fresh session when the first attempt is refused', 'keeps the edit and its step scope when the header start over is refused' (held draft GET), plus the extended 'does not open the review when the replacement session cannot be created'; FlowAIBuilderService.test.ts 'does not lend the saved-step scope to the session that replaced it'. Gate lane-reliability-npo-gate 4 -> 6 -> 7 (3-pass cap); the pass-3 blocker was fixed after the cap and landed as recorded residue with local verification, as the reviewer itself advised. Validation: ai-builder vitest 359 passed, svelte-check 0 errors, eslint/prettier clean, backend untouched. Follow-up: eneo-2jd.

title: Suggestion handoff message is Swedish-only and its order is built twice
description:
Found by the Codex commit gate (session review-suggestions-gate, iteration 22, 2026-09-06) while gating the batch handoff UI.

The server writes the canonical investigation message and ignores what the client sent (SendMessageRequest.canonical() -> investigation_message() in ai_builder_flow_review.py). Two consequences:

1. investigation_message() renders hard-coded Swedish regardless of the turn's ui_language, so an English user types nothing, sees an English optimistic message from the client, and after a refresh the persisted conversation shows Swedish.

2. The display text is constructed twice: the client builds a preview in flowReviewSuggestions.investigationMessage() in the response order and the active locale, while the server sorts and deduplicates the foci canonically before rendering. For a batch the two can disagree in item order, so the optimistic message and the persisted one differ.

Codex's smallest correction: have the server render the requested UI language and align ordering, or return the canonical display message so the client stops duplicating its construction. The second is the better shape - one owner for the sentence - but it changes the send response, so it wants its own slice.

Not urgent: the product is Swedish-first and the mismatch is cosmetic, but an English tenant sees a Swedish sentence in their own conversation.
close_reason: Fixed on tidy by 02dcc63eb (a parallel session): the screen and the server now compose the same sentence from the same fixed parts in the request's UI language, over one canonical deduplicated and ordered set of suggestions, so the optimistic text, the fingerprint and the retained message agree. Nothing left to do.

title: Review session permission does not survive conversation compaction
description:
Found by the Codex commit gate (session review-suggestions-gate, pass 15, 2026-09-06) on feature/ai-builder-review-suggestions.

The AI Builder review permission (flows_ai_builder_review / FlowApiAction.BUILDER_REVIEW) is decided per turn from a retained user message that names a review: conversation_acts_on_a_review() in ai_builder_conversation_metadata.py, used at both decision points in ai_builder_router.send_message. Conversation compaction keeps required units, preferred schema sources and a bounded tail (ai_builder_conversation_compaction.py, _required_message_indices), and review references are not among the required owners. A review outlives the turn that opened it by design, so a long enough review conversation loses its only marker and subsequent turns fall back to ordinary Builder authorization while still being a review-derived session.

This is pre-existing: before the 2026-09-06 slice the same decision was made from latest_user_review_context(), which has the same dependency on a retained message. The slice neither caused nor worsened it.

Do NOT fix by pinning the review message in _required_message_indices: test_the_floor_survives_the_real_compactor_dropping_the_review_message asserts that compaction drops the review message deliberately, and that the evidence floor survives because every accepted turn re-writes EVIDENCE_FLOOR_METADATA_KEY into the bounded tail. That is the established pattern for a fact that must outlive compaction, and it is the model to follow: carry a durable 'this session acts on a review' marker on every accepted turn's metadata the same way the floor is carried. Note that the floor itself is not a substitute, because metadata_for_user_message only writes it when it is non-zero, so a review over level-0 evidence writes none.

Acceptance: a review session compacted past its opening turn still requires BUILDER_REVIEW on the next turn, with a test that drives the real compactor.

title: Builder fixed values: classify every numeric constant as invariant, policy or delete
description: Owner rule 2026-09-06: no fixed values that give no benefit; Eneo is model agnostic; features must work with every model. The 16k evidence ceiling was one such value (deleted). Inventory of the Builder's numeric constants (rg over backend/src/eneo/flows/ai_builder) grouped by a first reading; each needs a written disposition beside it, then the deletions/derivations land as slices. (A) storage/protocol/safety bounds, keep fixed with a domain name and the reason: BUILDER_PROPOSAL_PAYLOAD_CAP_BYTES, MAX_SESSION_MESSAGE(S)/CONVERSATION_BYTES, error contract lengths, SCHEMA_MAX_JSON_BYTES/DEPTH, MAX_PROPOSAL_STEPS, MAX_STRUCTURED_FIELD_DEPTH, _SEND_LOCK_RELEASE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, PROVIDER_TOOL_CALL_ID_MAX_LENGTH, MAX_WINDOW_DAYS. (B) evidence/prompt sizing heuristics that should derive from the model window or the request budget, or be measured and justified: AI_BUILDER_RENDERED_EVIDENCE_MAX_CHARS=80, _MAX_TEMPLATE_PLACEHOLDER_EVIDENCE=8, _MAX_VISIBLE_EXAMPLE_EVIDENCE=8, _MAX_CLASSIFICATION_TRANSCRIPT_SOURCES=120, _MAX_CLASSIFICATION_STRUCTURED_VALUE_CHARS=500, MAX_QUOTE_CHARS=200, MAX_RATIONALE_CHARS=400, SCHEMA_FIELD_PROJECTION_MAX_ITEMS=8, EXAMPLE_OUTPUT_MAX_JSON_BYTES, the 15-entry cap in small_ref_enum_for_kind. (C) review/cohort shape: MAX_SUGGESTIONS=6, MAX_SOURCES_PER_SUGGESTION=3, MAX_SUGGESTION_STEPS=10, MAX_SUGGESTION_SAMPLE_RUNS=3, SAMPLE_COMPLETED_RUNS=2, SAMPLE_FAILED_RUNS=1, COHORT_SCAN/COMPLETED/FAILED_LIMIT, STEP_SHARE_THRESHOLD=0.5, MAX_REVIEW_FINDINGS_PER_TURN=10, MAX_REVIEWABLE_STEPS=40, READ_DEADLINE_SECONDS=20: decide which are tenant policy, which derive from the window, which are UI shape. (D) turn control: MAX_PROPOSAL_PROVIDER_CALLS=4, MAX_TEMPLATE_PREPARATION_STAGES: justify with the failure ladders or make policy. (E) language heuristics (clause segmenter windows, negation look-around words, section confidence counts): a different class (text rules), review with the A0 evidence, not this pass. title: After the Builder creates a flow you land on 'Grundinställningar', not on the steps you just approved
description: Found live 2026-09-14 on a from-scratch create journey. After approving a 4-step plan and confirming 'Skapa flödet', the app opens the new flow's editor at stage 1 'Grundinställningar' (aria-current=step), which asks for name and description, both of which the Builder just filled in. The user has spent the whole journey reviewing steps and is dropped on the one stage that has nothing to do with them; the steps they approved are two stages away under 'Bearbetningssteg'. Decide the right landing after an AI create (the steps stage, or a short 'what happens now' with Publicera as the single next action) and make focus land on it. Same question for landing after an AI edit is applied.
